title: Q1 2024 recon SLA review
subtitle: Helen wants match complete by 7:20pm ET. We hit 7:31 on month-end. Decision: 7:35 official on month-end, 7:20 other settlement days. Weekends still out of scope; she still asked. Action items below, not a transcript.
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Helen Cho, Marcus Bell, Priya Nair, Rahul Deshmukh, Aman Kumar (attendees); Kavya Menon, Diego Alvarez, Chris Patel (action owners not in room)
owners: Aman Kumar (notes), Rahul Deshmukh (SLA doc), Priya Nair (eng commitments)
summary: Quarterly SLA review for Clearhaven recon, March 12, 2024, 11:00-12:10 ET. Attendees: Helen Cho, Marcus Bell, Priya Nair, Rahul Deshmukh, Aman Kumar. We reviewed February close times, the January 31 7:31pm miss against Helen's 7:20 target, and Kafka ingest numbers since the April 2023 cutover. Decision in the room: official match-complete SLA is 7:20pm ET on regular settlement days and 7:35pm ET on month-end settlement days, measured as match-engine last commit for that day's settlement_date. Open: whether Saturday or Sunday windows are ever in-scope (they are not today; Helen asked again). Action items at the bottom with owners. These are notes, not a transcript, and not a new contract until Rahul updates the one-pager Marcus sends to Clearhaven legal.

blocks.text: Meeting

March 12, 2024, 11:00-12:10 ET, Zoom. Recurring quarterly SLA for the recon platform we run for Clearhaven Markets. Last one was December 7, 2023 (CLH-MTG-2023-062, I did not take those notes; Rahul did; I pulled numbers from his sheet). This round was scheduled because Helen wanted the 7:20pm line written down before April month-end, and because January 31 closed at 7:31pm ET, which she has mentioned in three standups.

blocks.label: SLA decision
blocks.text: Match-complete clock: last recon.match_result commit for settlement_date = that business day, as seen on pg-recon-01. Regular settlement days: 7:20pm ET. Month-end settlement days (last US business day of the calendar month, and any early-close day RailClear names by 10:00 ET): 7:35pm ET. Both are official, not best effort. Freeze 16:00-21:00 ET on settlement days stays. Weekends remain out of scope unless a separate ticket names a Saturday window 5 days ahead. Rahul updates the one-pager by March 22. Marcus sends it to Clearhaven legal. Helen will still ask about weekends; the answer in this meeting is no, with an open item to write the no down so we stop relitigating it every quarter.

Priya said 7:35 on month-end is the number we can defend with current match-engine capacity (6 pods, April 28 2023-shaped 8.2M peak still the planning case, February 29 2024 was 6.4M and closed 7:22). She would not sign 7:20 on month-end without a capacity project Rahul has not funded. Helen accepted 7:35 after looking at the January 31 trace. She did not accept 'best effort 7:20, we usually make it.' She wants a number she can tell her desk. 7:35 is that number on month-end. 7:20 stays on the other days, where we have been inside it 19 of 21 February settlement days, the two misses being 7:24 (Feb 13, MM2 stall 6.8 minutes) and 7:21 (Feb 21, flyway 121 + deploy that started 15:44 and canary-finished 16:01, which is the freeze SOP working as designed and still costing us a minute).
What we looked at

Chris's sheet: recon.sla_close_time, populated from match_result max(committed_at) per settlement_date, converted to America/New_York. I trust this more than Grafana wall clocks because the matcher can finish a minute after the dashboard panel 5-minute scrape. January and February 2024, plus December 2023 for the previous quarter comparison. Kafka ingest has been primary since April 11, 2023; FTP is fallback only and was not used in this quarter except a January 8 drill Diego ran at 10:20 that Helen was warned about.

blocks.text: Read of the table in the room: regular days are a 7:20 SLA we mostly hit. The misses are ingest stalls and deploy timing, both already owned (Diego's MM2 probe, SOP freeze). Month-end is a different distribution. January 31 at 7:31 is the one Helen filed as a miss against a target we had never signed. December 29 at 7:27 and February 29 at 7:22 are the same shape, smaller. If we sign 7:20 on month-end we will miss it as a matter of capacity, not as a surprise. If we sign 7:35 we would have hit all three month-ends in the sheet. That is why 7:35 exists.
January 31, the one she keeps citing

I walked the trace. Bus publish for the 18:15-18:30 window finished 18:31:14. ingest-bus-consumer lag peaked at 41k messages, recovered 18:34:02. match-engine write p95 1.12s from 18:40-19:10 while autovacuum ran on fact_leg_p20240131 (Rina's graph, freeze_age 186M, she has since set scale_factor 0.02 on children). Last match commit 19:31:08 ET, which is 7:31pm. Break-svc open-queue lag was fine; Helen's pain was the desk asking her at 7:22 whether they were done. They were not. No incident ticket because nothing crashed. That gap, 'late but not an incident,' is what she wants the SLA to cover. Fair.

Priya asked whether more match-engine pods would have hit 7:20 that day. Chris's back-of-envelope: 8 pods instead of 6, maybe 6-8 minutes off the tail, so 7:23-7:25, still not 7:20, and we pay for 8 pods every quiet Tuesday. She is not buying 8 pods for a 7:20 month-end until FY25 capacity (Rahul's CLH-MEM-2024-018 is not written yet; this is the seed). 7:35 plus Rina's vacuum tune is the 2024 answer. I will still ask Kavya for a partition-local vacuum schedule so 18:40 does not collide with the tail of match. That is an action, not a promise of 7:20.
Kafka ingest, since someone always asks if we should go back to files

Marcus asked, because someone on his side asked him, whether file drop would have been more predictable on January 31. No. File drop p50 emit-to-match in January 2023 was 40.2 minutes. We would have closed after 8pm on an 8.04M day. Bus p50 emit-to-match in February 2024 is 7.4 minutes on regular days, 11.8 on February 29. We are not reopening CLH-MEM-2023-004. I said that once. Rahul said it again. Helen did not ask; she likes the bus. Marcus needed the sentence for his email.

blocks.text: Replay button, because it changes the SLA clock

CLH-PRD-2024-002 is in flight (NS-RECON-612). Helen asked whether a replay at 6:50pm that finishes at 7:18 counts as making 7:20. Decision: the SLA clock is last commit for the settlement_date, including replay batches with replay_of set. If she replays at 7:10 and it finishes at 7:28 on a regular day, that is a miss. If she replays at 6:40 and it finishes at 7:12, that is a hit. We will not invent a second clock for 'first-pass complete.' She agreed, then asked for a dashboard panel that shows first-pass vs including-replay so she can tell her desk which it is. Chris will add it. The contractual number remains last commit.

Mean time to replay is still 47.3 minutes because the button is not in prod. Target under 8 is still the PRD success metric, separate from this SLA. Do not mix them in the one-pager. Rahul will keep them on two lines. Maya's no-edit constraint does not affect the clock.
Weekends (open, again)

Helen asked whether Saturday was in-scope. RailClear does not publish a Saturday settlement window in the current contract Marcus has. We do not run match-engine at 6 pods on Saturday. On-call is Diego's weekend rotation for pages, not for a 7:20 close. She asked because on Saturday March 2 a desk head wanted a 'what-if' replay of Friday's file against a corrected position snapshot. We did that as a ticketed one-off, finished 11:40am Saturday, no SLA. She wants the ability to request a Saturday window. Priya: 5 business days notice, a named NS-CHG, on-call engineer paid, SLA for that window negotiated in the ticket (not 7:20 by default, because ingest volume and staffing are weekday). Helen: she will still ask in the moment. We will still say no unless the ticket exists. This remains OPEN because Marcus thinks their legal will want a sentence, and the sentence is not written.

blocks.label: Open: weekend scope
blocks.text: Not in-scope today. Helen will ask again. Owner of the written sentence: Marcus Bell + Rahul, due March 22 with the one-pager. Owner of the operational path if they ever say yes: Priya (staffing) and Diego (do we even run MM2 on Saturday? today we do, at reduced alert). Do not quietly staff a Saturday 7:20 without a ticket.
Error budget and freeze, intersection with SLA

Diego was not in the room. I restated CLH-SOP-2023-019: no deploys 16:00-21:00 ET settlement days. Helen wants that to stay. February 21's 7:21 close was a canary that kissed the freeze. Priya will tell engineers 14:00 is the last start on regular days, 12:00 on month-end Fridays. That 12:00 month-end freeze start was an open question in the SOP; we closed it in this meeting. Month-end Friday freeze starts 12:00 ET. I will patch the SOP. Diego can object by Friday; if he does not, it is in.

Error budget abort during a canary can delay a fix that would have saved a close. That trade is accepted. We do not spend budget at 15:50 to maybe close at 7:19. We miss by a minute and keep the budget for an actual incident at 18:00. Helen preferred that when I put it that way. Marcus asked if error budget was in the customer-facing one-pager. No. Internal only. Do not put burn-rate math in the legal doc.
What we are not changing

items: Measurement stays last match_result commit on pg-recon-01 for that settlement_date, America/New_York. Not Grafana. Not Helen's dashboard scrape. Chris's job recon.sla_close_time is the source if we argue.

Break aging is not this SLA. Open-break count at 7:20 is a desk metric Helen owns. We did not sign a number for it. She can bring one next quarter if she wants, with a definition that excludes replay-induced duplicates (checker in the replay PRD).
ingest-api HTTP SLO is not this meeting. Different doc, Diego.
No return to 15-minute FTP as primary.

No 60-second FTP poller (still rejected, CLH-MEM-2023-004). Marcus's side suggested it as a month-end 'safety.' I said no in the room. Priya backed it. If they want a safety it is the FTP fallback we already have, not a new poller.
Payload edit in replay UI still no (Maya).

blocks.text: Rejected in the room

Helen's opening position was 7:20 every day including month-end, with us eating the capacity cost. Rejected. Capacity is not funded, January 31 would still have been a miss even at 8 pods on Chris's envelope, and signing a number we will miss is how Marcus gets a penalty clause. Priya will not sign a penalty on 7:20 month-end. Marcus said there is no penalty clause today and he does not want to invent one. Good.

Rahul floated 7:30 every day as a single number, simpler one-pager. Helen rejected. Regular days we already hit 7:20 and she does not want the desk to slide to 7:30 because the paper said they could. Split number it is: 7:20 / 7:35. The one-pager can have two rows.
Marcus floated '7:20 with a 15-minute grace on month-end' as wording. That is 7:35 with extra steps. We picked the honest number. No grace language. Official 7:35 ME.

blocks.label: Rejected: single 7:20 including month-end
blocks.text: Not funded, not hit on January 31 even with a hopeful extra two pods, and it would put a miss on the books every busy close. 7:35 ME is the signed number. Do not 'try for 7:20' in status reports as if it were the SLA; Helen will quote the report back to us.
Capacity and Rina

Rina Das was not in the meeting. I owe her a summary. January 31 autovacuum on the daily child collided with the match tail. She already dropped scale_factor on children after CLH-TDD-2023-011. She asked in Slack on February 1 whether we wanted a quiet period 18:30-19:10 with vacuum_cost_delay raised. I had not answered. Answering is an action: yes, on month-end only, she gets a 40-minute quieter vacuum, we accept slightly more bloat until 22:30. Aman to send that yes by March 15. If she says the quieter vacuum risks wraparound, we listen and do not force it.

8.2M peak remains the planning case even though February 29 was 6.41M. Rahul will not rebase the capacity memo on a quiet February. April and July month-ends are the ones that look like 8M. We keep 8.2M in the heads.
How we will report this quarter

Chris will extend recon.sla_close_time with a column sla_due (19:20 or 19:35 local, stored as timestamptz) and sla_hit boolean. #clh-recon gets a bot line at close: '2024-03-12 close 19:04 ET, SLA 19:20, HIT.' Month-end the line says SLA 19:35. Helen wants the bot. Diego's Slack app can do it; I will not build a second bot. If the bot is late, the table is still the source.

After that the notes are the record. Helen already corrected 7:31 vs 7:29; that correction is in v1.0. Further corrections need a timestamp.
Appendix: definition of match-complete, so we stop arguing in June

Match-complete is the timestamptz of the last INSERT or UPDATE on recon.match_result where settlement_date equals the business day's settlement_date, as committed on pg-recon-01 primary, converted to America/New_York. It includes rows from replay batches. It excludes rows for other settlement dates that happen to commit in the same hour (yesterday's leftover is yesterday's clock). It excludes break_header writes. It excludes staging. If the primary is in a failover at 7:18, we use the replica time only if Rina says the replica was caught up; otherwise the clock waits for the primary. That edge case has not happened on a close. Diego's failover runbook should mention it; I will ping him, not invent the wording here.

Month-end settlement day is the last day RailClear publishes a full window for that calendar month. Usually last US business day. If they publish an early close, Helen tells #clh-recon by 10:00 ET and 7:35 applies. If she tells us at 15:00, 7:20 still applies and we try anyway. That asymmetry is intentional. We will not move the SLA with three hours of notice on a regular Thursday.

Regular settlement day is any other day they publish. Not weekends. Not US holidays when they do not publish. If they publish on a holiday we did not staff, that is an incident and a ticket, not an automatic 7:20. Priya was explicit. Marcus nodded. Write it down, which is what this paragraph is.
